options.text: True positives over everyone who has the disease
True positives over every positive test
True negatives over every negative test
A number that falls when the disease gets rarer

questions.explanation: Sensitivity starts from people who have the disease. Predictive values start from the test result.

questions.stem: The disease gets rarer. Which number falls?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity and specificity stay put. The room changes the predictive value.

questions.stem: A test is 90% sensitive and 90% specific. In a room of 10 people with the disease and 90 without, a positive test means:
questions.explanation: Nine true positives and nine false positives. 9 / 18 = 50%. 90% is the sensitivity, not the meaning of a yes in this room.

questions.stem: In that same room, a negative test is about:
questions.explanation: 81 true negatives and 1 false negative. 81 / 82 is about 99%.

questions.stem: Control risk 10%, treatment risk 6%. The absolute risk reduction is:
questions.explanation: 10% minus 6% is 4 percentage points. 40% is the relative reduction.

questions.stem: That same trial. The relative risk reduction is:
questions.explanation: 4 percentage points divided by the control risk of 10% is 40%.

questions.stem: Control 10%, treatment 6%. Number needed to treat?
questions.explanation: 1 / 0.04 = 25. Three is one over the relative reduction, rounded up, and that is the trap.

questions.stem: The number needed to treat is built from:
questions.explanation: NNT = 1 / ARR. The relative reduction looks larger and is the usual decoy.

questions.stem: If the number needed to treat comes out as a fraction, you:

options.text: Round up to the next whole person

questions.explanation: A part of a person cannot be treated, so you round up.

options.text: Sensitivity and specificity do not move with prevalence.
Predictive values move with the room you are standing in.
A large relative reduction always means a small number needed to treat.
A rare disease makes a positive test a weaker yes.

questions.explanation: The number needed to treat follows the absolute, not the relative, reduction.
